info.text:
The health plan with the lower premium can cost you more.
Premium x 12 + your share of care = what a plan really costs in a year.
Example: a $40/month plan beats a $120/month plan in a $500 year ($980 vs $1,940), but loses by $1,440 in a $20,000 year ($6,880 vs $5,440).
Premiums don't count toward the out-of-pocket max.
In 2025, 34% of covered workers had a single deductible of $2,000+ (average single deductible: $1,886).
Sources: KFF 2025 Employer Health Benefits Survey; HealthCare.gov. Plans in the example are hypothetical.
News and education, not financial advice.
